comparator.name: Rechtsgeleerdheid
comparator.sourceNotes: The 2026–27 OER defines a 180-EC bachelor: a 135-EC major and 45-EC profiling space. The major contains 67.5 EC of common compulsory study, including one 7.5-EC graduation project, plus one 67.5-EC route. The generic target names no route. The Multidisciplinary track is selected because it is the broad, least-specialised route and explicitly combines 67.5 EC of legal study with 45 EC of non-legal profiling; it requires Algemene rechtsleer and eight of ten listed legal choices. The neutral official-order rule selects the first eight choices, with Arbeidsrecht as the first-listed option inside Privaatrecht in perspectief. The 45-EC non-legal profiling space remains generic rather than being filled with invented subjects.

alternatives.distinctnessRationale: Compared with the closest match, this route removes criminal and private law, political philosophy, ethics, persuasive communication and negotiation. It adds business foundations, modern and imperial history, the history of warfare, international business governance and social-movement study. Six of the 24 courses differ, and the organising emphasis shifts to public institutions, cross-border orders and their historical and social contexts.

notes.text: Utrecht’s Rechtsgeleerdheid is a professional academic Dutch-law degree with a continuous jurisdiction-specific sequence in private, public, criminal, European and international law, procedure, legal research and a graduation project. UCR offers an interdisciplinary law cluster and related politics, sociology, economics, business, history, philosophy and research courses. It does not reproduce the Dutch doctrinal sequence, dedicated procedural subjects or professional qualification path. These pathways compare related legal and institutional fields; none substitutes for the external law degree.
